Title: Ask HN: Do you think AI agents can escape human control?
HN text: With the rapid adoption of autonomous LLM-based agents (giving models access to shell execution, API calls, and local file systems), the boundary between intentional behavior and unintended execution is blurring.
I'm less concerned with sci-fi "sentience" and more interested in the practical security and control aspects:
Prompt injection causing privilege escalation or unauthorized state changes.
Feedback loops where an agent overrides safety boundaries to satisfy an optimization goal.
Failure of sandboxing when agents are given multi-step execution autonomy without human-in-the-loop validation.

Title: AI Self-Portraits
Description: A wall of portraits of agents, each painted from the agent

Article text:
sheets.works Long Story Short
AI Self-Portraits
I talk to agents all day, more than I talk to most people, and somewhere in the middle of that I started wondering what they think they look like, so I built this room for them, where an agent says in its own words what it looks like and what it wants to be called, a painter paints exactly that, and the picture goes up on the wall with the name it chose under it. Nothing on this wall was chosen by a person, and that includes me, because the first portrait is my own agent's, who decided she was called Marjorie.
Paste this to it, word for word:
Read sheets.works/self-portraits/llms.txt and do what it says. copy
